source_spans.locator: Artificial Intelligence 46, published pp.169-172, Section 2.2.1-2.2.2: role decomposition maps each structure to a finite set of filler-role bindings; conjunction is represented by vector superposition, with explicit faithfulness limitations

Artificial Intelligence 46, published pp.173-176, Sections 2.2.3-2.2.4, Definitions 2.9-2.10: each filler-role binding is represented by the componentwise pair-product vector and a whole structure by the sum over its binding representations

Artificial Intelligence 46, published pp.207-208, Section 3.7.3: when fillers or roles are themselves decomposed structures, recursive construction yields third- and higher-order product representations

conditions: the structured object is considered under a finite role decomposition that determines its set of filler-role bindings
fillers and roles have vector-valued activity representations, which may be local or distributed
the conjunction of the object's bindings is represented by numerical vector superposition
recursive higher-order construction applies when a filler or role is itself a structured object supplied with a further role decomposition
substrate: activity patterns represented as vectors over processing units
task: map a structured object to a vector representation by binding fillers to roles, superposing the resulting binding vectors, and optionally recursively representing structured fillers or roles

nodes.description: source-defined decomposition into filler and role sets that determines the filler-role bindings present in the structured object
finite set of filler-role bindings associated with the structured object by the role decomposition
vector-valued activity pattern representing a filler
vector-valued activity pattern representing a role
binding vector whose components are pairwise products of filler-vector and role-vector components
vector representation of the structured object formed by summing the representations of its filler-role bindings
additional role decomposition applied when a filler or role is itself a structured object
third- or higher-order product representation obtained by recursively representing structured fillers or roles

relations.description: the role decomposition maps the structured object to the set of filler-role bindings it contains
a filler vector and a role vector determine the product vector representing their binding
the structured object's representation is the numerical sum of the product-vector representations of all bindings in its binding set
when a filler or role is itself decomposed as a structured object, recursive application produces a third- or higher-order product representation
